title: Conditions Governing Two or More Air Ticket Fare Brands Bookings in One Traveller's Name
content:
A traveller may hold any number of Air Ticket Fare Brands bookings at the same time, and each booking carries its own fare brand, its own money and its own terms. No ceiling stands on the number of bookings one traveller may hold at once.

## 1. Duplicate bookings

1.1 Two bookings for the same traveller on the same routing and the same departure date are treated as a duplicate.
1.2 The later of the two bookings is opened, then referred for duplicate review before it is ticketed, because airlines refuse duplicate tickets in one name.
1.3 A duplicate is judged on the routing and the departure date together. Two bookings that share a routing but depart on different dates are not duplicates of one another, and neither are two bookings that share a departure date on different routings.

## 2. No aggregation between bookings

2.1 Nothing in these conditions aggregates the terms of two bookings. A benefit earned on one booking is never spent on another, except through the travel-credit account, which is governed separately.
2.2 It follows that the fare brand of one booking never reaches another booking's money, and that two bookings held in one name are priced, reworked and closed each on its own terms.

## 3. Matrix of two bookings in one name

| Same routing | Same departure date | Treatment of the later booking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | a duplicate: opened, then referred for duplicate review before ticketing |
| yes | no | not a duplicate |
| no | yes | not a duplicate |
| no | no | not a duplicate |

## 4. Hypothetical illustration

A traveller holds a Basic Economy Lite booking and an Economy Flex booking on the same routing departing on the same day. The second is a duplicate and is referred for duplicate review before it is ticketed. Whichever is eventually ticketed keeps its own brand's terms: the conditions above give the Economy Flex booking no claim on the Basic Economy Lite booking's money, and no claim the other way.
